item.title: Top U.N. court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
item.description:
Judgment finds ‘intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population’ after case seen as critical test for dealing with most serious of state crimes Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority in its 2016-17 military campaign, the world’s highest court has ruled. The judgment from the international court of justice (ICJ) – which has never previously found a state responsible for genocide – ends a seven-year legal battle that was seen as a critical global test for dealing with the most serious of all state crimes. item.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 has reached 1 light-day from Earth, the first human-made object in space to reach that distance
item.description:
This illustration shows Voyager 1 passing by the rings of Saturn. NASA/Hulton Archive/Getty Images In the summer of 2027, the Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 spacecraft will each reach a milestone in time. On Sept. 5 and Aug. 20, respectively, they will each have spent 50 years in space . During their journeys, they first explored the planets of the outer solar system, then traveled to the edge of the solar system. Eventually, they passed into the interstellar medium : the space between stars. Although not the first spacecraft ever launched, these are now the two oldest spacecraft still operating. But before the spacecraft hit their semicentennial, Voyager 1 will also reach a milestone in distance. On Nov. 18, 2026, at 5:16 a.m. EST, Voyager 1 will become the first human-built object of any kind to reach a distance of one light-day from Earth . At that point, it will have traveled about 16…

item.title: In an authoritarian economy, Jensen Huang may be too big to fail | Robert Reich
item.description:
Nvidia posted a stronger-than-expected third quarter and a bullish outlook in its first earnings report after Jensen Huang was ousted as CEO in a scandal that has reportedly spawned an SEC investigation. On the company's earnings call, newly appointed chairman Harvey Jones said the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," despite a movement among some employees and investors to bring him back. Why it matters: Nvidia remains squarely at the center of the AI economy — and investors are anxious for guidance on the company's strategic roadmap following Huang's sudden exit. Zoom in: Nvidia recorded quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion and net income of $65.3 billion, both more than doubling its performance from a year earlier. item.title: South Korea tightens security for national exam over AI cheating scandal
item.description:
South Korea has been gripped by revelations of AI-aided cheating, just days before more than half a million students are to sit high-stakes entrance exams The integrity of South Korea’s career-defining university entrance exam has been thrown into doubt after the top scorer in a recent professional exam admitted using a concealed camera and AI to cheat. On Thursday, more than half a million people, mostly school students, are due to sit the exam, known as the suneung, at 1,312 centres across the country. The exam runs for a gruelling eight hours over a single day and determines which university a candidate can attend and, in turn, their future prospects. Continue reading...

item.description:
In a time of national dislocation, America needs what President Ronald Reagan once delivered in his own day: renewed military power joined to a free-market economy and the first principles that make our country exceptional. item.title: It Feels Like Everything is Breaking, and It’s Not Even Hackers
item.description:
You know things are bad when panic-buyers start emptying the shelves at Costco. As you might have noticed, everything is breaking. Over the past week, Outlook has gone down, U.S. air traffic control has gone down, banking systems have gone down, and the National Security Agency’s confidential-telephone system has gone down, and just today, Apple announced that some of its services are down. There is an air of something nefarious afoot. “If this is all a coincidence,” Senator Josh Hawley of Missouri said yesterday, “it’s like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world.” Others have traded apocalyptic theories: Are rogue AI agents taking over everything? item.title: What is a ‘nuclear briefcase’, spotted at the APEC summit?
item.description:
Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin are holding their first-ever trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the APEC forum. It is a historic moment in more ways than one, with the leaders of the world’s three most powerful countries around the same table. Ukraine, the war in Iran, nuclear disarmament and artificial intelligence are all expected to be discussed, and the summit has stoked fears of a carve-up of the world into spheres of influence. But despite the buzz, analysts expect more symbolism than substance, with few concrete breakthroughs likely. Our correspondent in the region has more.

Sources: Al Jazeera English, France 24

item.title: Florida pastor found guilty over role in assassination of Haitian president
item.description:
Christian Emmanuel Sanon faces life in prison after conviction on charges arising from killing of Jovenel Moïse A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted on Wednesday of US charges arising from the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse. Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty on charges including conspiring to kill Moïse after a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami. He had faced a total of eight charges including conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the United States. Continue reading...
